issues.current_text: O Brent fechou a US$103,14, maior patamar em três anos.
issues.previous_text: Brent por volta de $100/barril — alta de 50% em um mês
issues.suggestion: Brent price as headline anchor appears in 03-12 ('Brent oscila em torno de $100'), 03-13 ('Brent por volta de $100/barril'), and now 03-14. The $103 level is genuinely new, but the 'Brent hits new high' frame is wearing thin across four consecutive editions. Vary the angle — lead with the downstream impact (shipping insurance rates, refinery margins, consumer prices) instead of the barrel price.

issues.current_text: a pior crise marítima desde a Segunda Guerra
issues.previous_text: a maior liberação coordenada de petróleo da história
issues.suggestion: Superlative + historical comparison ('worst X since Y', 'largest X in history') is becoming a crutch. Used on 03-11 ('maior liberação da história') and now 03-14 ('pior crise desde a Segunda Guerra'). Cut the historical comparison or use a concrete metric instead — '3,000 ships stranded' already conveys the scale without the superlative.

Vary the sentence structure: lead with what the company does or why it matters, not the funding amount. Reserve the 'raised $X at $Y valuation' phrasing for at most one deal per edition.

issues.suggestion: Every subtitle uses the same three-clause, comma-separated structure. This is the fourth consecutive edition with this exact pattern. Break the rhythm — try a single declarative sentence, a question, or a two-part structure.

summary: Moderate repetition. Two stories (IEA 400M barrel release, Russian oil sanctions waiver) are re-reported without new developments. The Pakistan-Afghanistan Kam Air bombing and Section 301 tariffs repeat prior coverage with thin new angles. The 'Brent at record high' and 'startup raises $X at $Y valuation' frames are wearing thin across four consecutive editions.
